title: When Was Claude Released? Every Claude Release Date, 2023 to 2026
summary: Claude first launched March 14, 2023. Get every Claude release date through Sonnet 5.5 (Sep 28, 2026), with launch prices, context windows and retirements.
body_markdown:
Claude was first released on March 14, 2023, when Anthropic opened early access to Claude and Claude Instant through a chat interface and an API. The newest Claude, Claude Sonnet 5.5, came out on September 28, 2026, and between those two dates Anthropic shipped a new Claude model on 24 separate days.


That is the whole answer to "when was Claude released?" The rest of this guide is the reference behind it. It holds the dated ledger of every Claude release, the price and context window each model launched with, which launches still work today, and how fast the cadence is accelerating. Every date below comes from Anthropic's own announcement pages, its model deprecations page, or its pricing and models documentation, checked on September 29, 2026.


> **TL;DR:** Claude first launched on **March 14, 2023** with limited access, opened to the public at claude.ai with Claude 2 on **July 11, 2023** , and has had 24 dated launches since, most recently **Sonnet 5.5 on September 28, 2026** . Opus 5.5 shipped September 22. Haiku 5.5 is next.Jump to the ledger ↓


A release date does not tell you whether a model builds a working app, so the[TSK-1 Benchmark](https://www.taskade.com/tsk) sends the same app request to each model and records whether the app worked, and the[Claude results](https://www.taskade.com/tsk/claude) show how each Claude model did.


---


## When Was Claude Released? The Quick Answer


**Claude was first released on March 14, 2023, first opened to the public on July 11, 2023, and most recently updated on September 28, 2026 with Claude Sonnet 5.5.** Which date you mean depends on what "released" means to you: the first announcement, the first time a stranger could sign up, or the newest model on the API today.


Question Date Model What happened


First Claude ever released March 14, 2023 Claude 1 and Claude Instant Early access through a chat interface and an API after a closed alpha with partners


First Claude open to the public July 11, 2023 Claude 2 Beta chat at claude.ai for the US and UK, plus API access for businesses


First Claude with a 200K context window November 21, 2023 Claude 2.1 200,000 tokens, tool use in beta and system prompts


First three-tier family March 4, 2024 Claude 3 Opus, Sonnet and Haiku Opus and Sonnet the same day, Haiku on March 13


Claude Code first appears February 24, 2025 Claude 3.7 Sonnet Limited research preview of the command-line agent


Claude 4 family May 22, 2025 Opus 4 and Sonnet 4 Claude Code became generally available the same day


Latest Opus September 22, 2026 Claude Opus 5.5 $4 input and $20 output per million tokens


Latest Sonnet September 28, 2026 Claude Sonnet 5.5 $2 input and $10 output per million tokens


Latest Haiku October 15, 2025 Claude Haiku 4.5 $1 input and $5 output. Haiku 5.5 is announced for the coming weeks


Latest Mythos-class public model September 1, 2026 Claude Fable 5.1 $10 input and $50 output. Mythos 5.1 is restricted


*Sources: Anthropic announcement pages for each model, linked in the year sections below, and the[models overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview) .*


### Why the answer is not one date


Anthropic did not launch Claude once. It launched a research assistant to a short list of partners in March 2023, a consumer product four months later, a tiered product line a year after that, and a coding agent in 2025. Each of those moments is a defensible answer, which is why the search results for this question disagree with each other.


The plain rule is this. If you need one date, use **March 14, 2023** . If you are citing when ordinary people could first chat with Claude, use **July 11, 2023** . If you are choosing a model to build on, use the ledger below and read the "status today" column.


```text
CLAUDE, IN FOUR DATES    2023-03-14   Claude 1 + Instant    Limited access, chat + API  |  2023-07-11   Claude 2              Public beta at claude.ai (US, UK)  |  2024-03-04   Claude 3 family       Opus / Sonnet / Haiku tiers begin  |  2026-09-28   Sonnet 5.5            Newest model on the API today
```


For the company behind those dates, including how Anthropic was founded and why it split from OpenAI, read the[full Anthropic and Claude company history](https://www.taskade.com/blog/anthropic-claude-history) . This guide stays on the models.


---

"Status today" comes from the[model deprecations page](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations) , and "not sooner than" is Anthropic's tentative retirement floor for a model that is still active.

The Claude 3.5 Haiku row uses the announcement date. Anthropic's post said the model would arrive later that month.*


Some rows deserve a footnote.


- **Claude 3 Sonnet's context window** matches Opus because Anthropic's Claude 3 post says all three models "will initially offer a 200K context window upon launch."
- **The Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 rows** say beta because Anthropic launched the 1M window in beta on the developer platform, at a premium price above 200K tokens for Opus 4.6. Anthropic's pricing page now says Claude 4.6 and later models carry the full 1M window at standard rates.
- **The Mythos Preview row** shows the price Project Glasswing participants pay. Anthropic said it did not plan to make Mythos Preview generally available.
- **The Sonnet 5 row** launched at $2 / $10 as introductory pricing with a planned rise to $3 / $15 on September 1, 2026. Anthropic's pricing page now says that rise "will not occur."


### The lineage at a glance


The ledger is easier to read as five tracks. Opus, Sonnet and Haiku are the three tiers that Claude 3 introduced. Mythos-class models, the Mythos Preview and then Fable and Mythos, sit above Opus. The track lengths show which tier Anthropic updates most often.


Two things stand out. The Opus and Sonnet tracks moved together for most of the timeline, and the Haiku track is the slow one: three releases in more than two years, with Haiku 4.5 still current as of this writing. To choose between the tiers today, use the sibling guide,[Claude models explained](https://www.taskade.com/blog/claude-models-explained) , which covers effort levels, fallbacks and which model fits which job.


---


## 2023: From a Closed Alpha to a 200K Context Window


**Claude spent 2023 moving from a partner-only assistant to a public product with the largest context window on the market, in three launches: March 14, July 11 and November 21.** The year set the pattern that still holds. Anthropic launches a model, names its context window as the headline, and frames safety as the differentiator.


2023 launch Date What shipped Headline claim


Claude 1 and Claude Instant Mar 14 Chat interface and API, early access Helpful, honest and harmless assistant


100K context window May 11 Context grew from 9,000 to 100,000 tokens in the API Roughly 75,000 words in one prompt


Claude 2 Jul 11 Public beta at claude.ai, API for businesses 76.5% on the bar exam multiple-choice section


Claude 2.1 Nov 21 200K context, tool use beta, system prompts 2x fewer false statements than Claude 2.0


*Sources: Anthropic's announcements for[Claude](https://www.anthropic.com/news/introducing-claude) ,[100K context windows](https://www.anthropic.com/news/100k-context-windows) ,[Claude 2](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-2) and[Claude 2.1](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-2-1) .*


### March 14, 2023: Claude and Claude Instant


Anthropic's first announcement called Claude "a next-generation AI assistant based on Anthropic's research into training helpful, honest, and harmless AI systems." It came in two versions: Claude, the high-performance model, and Claude Instant, "a lighter, less expensive, and much faster option." The company said it had run a closed alpha with partners and was now ready to offer Claude more broadly through early access requests.


That word "broadly" is easy to over-read. Claude in March 2023 was not something a curious person could sign up for that afternoon. It reached users through partners and early-access requests, which is why most timelines call it a limited launch. The announcement listed summarization, search, creative and collaborative writing, question answering and coding as the target jobs. It did not print a context window or a price in the text of the post.


The safety framing was already there. Anthropic described Claude as "much less likely to produce harmful outputs, easier to converse with, and more steerable." The method behind that claim, training a model against a written set of principles, is explained in our[Constitutional AI wiki entry](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/ai/constitutional-ai) .


### May 11, 2023: the first big context jump


Two months later, Anthropic announced that Claude's context window had grown from 9,000 tokens to 100,000 tokens in the API. Its own gloss was roughly 75,000 words, or about six hours of audio, and it said Claude could digest hundreds of pages of material in under a minute. This is the first of three big context steps in Claude's history, and the timeline of that whole race is in our[history of the context window](https://www.taskade.com/blog/context-window-history) .


### July 11, 2023: Claude 2 and the public launch


**Claude 2 is the release that made Claude a consumer product.** Anthropic opened a beta chat experience at claude.ai for users in the US and UK, and it made the API available to businesses at the same price as Claude 1.3. The company said global expansion would follow in the coming months.


Anthropic put numbers behind the upgrade. Claude 2 scored 76.5% on the multiple-choice section of the bar exam, up from 73.0%. It scored 71.2% on the HumanEval coding test, up from 56.0%, and 88.0% on the GSM8k math set, up from 85.2%. It accepted up to 100,000 tokens of input, and Anthropic called it twice as good as Claude 1.3 at giving harmless responses.


Treat those scores as launch-day claims from the vendor, not as neutral measurements. The tradition of every lab reporting its own best benchmark is a story of its own, told in[why every model claims to be best](https://www.taskade.com/blog/ai-benchmarks-history) .


### November 21, 2023: Claude 2.1


Claude 2.1 doubled the context window to **200,000 tokens** , which Anthropic put at about 150,000 words or more than 500 pages. It also introduced two features developers now take for granted: **system prompts** , so a builder can set standing instructions, and **tool use in beta** , so Claude could call developer-defined functions and APIs. Anthropic reported a 2x decrease in false statements compared with Claude 2.0.


The 200K window came with a catch that the announcement stated plainly. On claude.ai, the full window was reserved for Claude Pro subscribers. Free users kept the smaller one. That split, a bigger model or bigger window for paying subscribers first, has repeated in nearly every release since.


### What 2023 taught the market


By the end of 2023 Claude had a public chat product, a paid tier with a 200K window, system prompts and a tool-use beta. Each of those became a standard feature of the category. For the other side of that race, the parallel record is in our[OpenAI and ChatGPT history](https://www.taskade.com/blog/openai-chatgpt-history) and the[ChatGPT model list](https://www.taskade.com/blog/chatgpt-models) .


The retirement record for 2023 is short and complete. Anthropic told developers on September 4, 2024 that Claude 1 and the Instant models would retire on November 6, 2024, and on January 21, 2025 that Claude 2, Claude 2.1 and Claude 3 Sonnet (a 2024 model) would retire on July 21, 2025. Both retirements have happened. No 2023 model still answers on Anthropic's API.


---


## 2024: Claude 3 Turns One Model Into a Product Line


**In 2024 Anthropic replaced the single Claude with a three-tier family, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku, and released four times: March 4, March 13, June 20 and October 22.** The naming and the price ladder set in March 2024 are still the structure of the lineup, even though every 2024 model has since retired.


2024 launch Date Launch price (in / out) Headline claim


Claude 3 Opus and Sonnet Mar 4 $15 / $75 and $3 / $15 200K context, three tiers


Claude 3 Haiku Mar 13 $0.25 / $1.25 Fastest and cheapest of the family


Claude 3.5 Sonnet Jun 20 $3 / $15 2x the speed of Claude 3 Opus, plus Artifacts


Upgraded 3.5 Sonnet, 3.5 Haiku, computer use beta Oct 22 Haiku $0.80 / $4 (set Dec 3) Claude can operate a computer, in public beta


*Sources: Anthropic's announcements for[Claude 3](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-family) ,[Claude 3 Haiku](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-haiku) ,[Claude 3.5 Sonnet](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-5-sonnet) and[the 3.5 models and computer use](https://www.anthropic.com/news/3-5-models-and-computer-use) .*


### March 4, 2024: Claude 3


The Claude 3 announcement introduced three models in one post: Haiku, the fastest and most cost-effective, Sonnet, the balanced one, and Opus, the most intelligent. All three launched with a 200K context window, and Anthropic said some customers could get up to 1 million tokens. Prices set the ladder: Haiku at $0.25 and $1.25, Sonnet at $3 and $15, and Opus at $15 and $75 per million input and output tokens.


Opus and Sonnet were available on March 4. The announcement said Haiku would be available soon, and it arrived on March 13. That nine-day gap is the first example of a pattern that keeps recurring: a family announced together and shipped in stages, which is one reason a single "release date" for a model generation is often ambiguous.


The three-tier design is the lasting contribution. Before Claude 3 you picked Claude or Claude Instant. After it, you chose a point on a price and intelligence curve, which is exactly the decision the[Claude models explained](https://www.taskade.com/blog/claude-models-explained) guide walks through and the[Opus versus Sonnet comparison](https://www.taskade.com/compare/opus-vs-sonnet) prices out.


### June 20, 2024: Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Artifacts


Anthropic announced Claude 3.5 Sonnet on June 20, 2024, US time, as the first model in a 3.5 family. It kept Sonnet pricing at $3 and $15 per million tokens, kept the 200K window, and ran at twice the speed of Claude 3 Opus. It was free on claude.ai and the iOS app, with higher limits for Pro and Team subscribers.


It also launched **Artifacts** , a workspace that shows generated code and documents in a window beside the conversation so you can edit them live. Artifacts is the first time Claude's output lived beside the conversation instead of inside it. The same instinct, output that stays alive and editable after the chat ends, is what[Taskade Genesis](https://www.taskade.com/create?entry_kind=content&source=blog&entry=%2Fblog%2Fclaude-release-dates) builds around.


This is the row where the date is worth a footnote. Anthropic's announcement is dated June 20 in US time, and some pages and time zones show June 21. The ledger uses June 20.


### October 22, 2024: an upgraded Sonnet, Haiku 3.5 and computer use


Anthropic announced three things in one post: an upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet, a new Claude 3.5 Haiku, and a public beta of **computer use** , a capability that lets Claude perceive and interact with computer interfaces. Developers got computer use on the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud's Vertex AI the same day.


Anthropic was candid about its state. It called computer use "experimental, at times cumbersome and error-prone," and said it expected the capability to improve as developers gave feedback. Claude 3.5 Haiku was to be released "later this month." Its price was revised on December 3, 2024 to $0.80 input and $4 output per million tokens, which is the number the ledger shows.


Computer use was small at the time and large in hindsight. It set the direction for agent products: a model that acts, not just answers. Our[AI agents guide](https://www.taskade.com/blog/what-are-ai-agents) covers what that shift means in practice.


### What 2024 taught the market


Four launches in a year gave buyers a stable ladder. Opus was the ceiling, Sonnet the workhorse, and Haiku the cheap tier. The retirement notes for these models are on the deprecations page: Claude 3 Opus retired on January 5, 2026, both 3.5 Sonnet versions on October 28, 2025, and Claude 3.5 Haiku on February 19, 2026. Claude 3 Haiku lasted longest, retiring on April 20, 2026, more than two years after launch.


---


## 2025: Claude Code, Extended Thinking and the Claude 4 Series


**In 2025 Anthropic shipped six launches, February 24, May 22, August 5, September 29, October 15 and November 24, and turned Claude from a chat assistant into a coding agent.** The year's defining events were a command-line tool called Claude Code, the Claude 4 family, and a price cut on Opus that reset what a flagship model costs.


2025 launch Date Launch price (in / out) Headline claim


Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Claude Code preview Feb 24 $3 / $15 Visible step-by-step thinking, up to 128K thinking tokens


Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4 May 22 $15 / $75 and $3 / $15 Opus 4 at 72.5% on SWE-bench, Claude Code generally available


Claude Opus 4.1 Aug 5 same as Opus 4 74.5% on SWE-bench Verified


Claude Sonnet 4.5 Sep 29 $3 / $15 61.4% on OSWorld, Claude Agent SDK released


Claude Haiku 4.5 Oct 15 $1 / $5 Sonnet 4-level coding at one-third the cost


Claude Opus 4.5 Nov 24 $5 / $25 Opus price cut, new effort parameter


*Sources: Anthropic's announcements for[Claude 3.7 Sonnet](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-7-sonnet) ,[Claude 4](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-4) ,[Opus 4.1](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-4-1) ,[Sonnet 4.5](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-sonnet-4-5) ,[Haiku 4.5](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-haiku-4-5) and[Opus 4.5](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-4-5) .*


### February 24, 2025: Claude 3.7 Sonnet and the Claude Code preview


Claude 3.7 Sonnet kept the $3 and $15 price, which Anthropic said includes thinking tokens. Its new trick was a choice between near-instant responses and extended, step-by-step thinking that is made visible to the user. API users could set how long the model thinks, up to 128K tokens of reasoning. For a plain-language tour of what that means, see our guide to[AI thinking modes](https://www.taskade.com/blog/ai-thinking-modes-explained) .


The same post introduced **Claude Code** as a limited research preview: a command-line tool that lets developers delegate substantial coding tasks. Anthropic said early testing showed it completing in one pass tasks that would normally take 45 minutes or more of manual work. That is the launch date of the product whose whole story is told in[What is Claude Code?](https://www.taskade.com/blog/claude-code-history) .


### May 22, 2025: Claude 4


Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4 launched together. Anthropic called Opus 4 "the world's best coding model" and reported 72.5% on SWE-bench and 43.2% on Terminal-bench. Prices carried over from Claude 3: $15 and $75 for Opus, $3 and $15 for Sonnet. Both models added extended thinking with tool use in beta, so Claude could alternate between reasoning and calling tools such as web search, and both could run tools in parallel.


Claude Code moved from preview to **general availability** the same day, with new VS Code and JetBrains integrations and GitHub Actions support through the Claude Code SDK. If you want one date for "when did Claude become an agent product," May 22, 2025 is the strongest candidate.


### August 5, 2025: Opus 4.1


Opus 4.1 was a point release. Anthropic reported 74.5% on SWE-bench Verified, said the strengths were multi-file code refactoring and pinpointing precise corrections in large codebases, and kept pricing the same as Opus 4. It was the last Opus released at the $15 and $75 price. Anthropic's pricing page lists Opus 4.1 as retired on the Claude API, except on Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud, which set their own schedules.


### September 29, 2025: Sonnet 4.5 and the Agent SDK


Sonnet 4.5 kept the $3 and $15 price and posted 77.2% on SWE-bench Verified. Anthropic said it led the OSWorld computer-use benchmark at 61.4%, up from Sonnet 4's 42.2%, and that it could maintain focus for more than 30 hours on complex, multi-step tasks. The launch also released the **Claude Agent SDK** , the same infrastructure Anthropic uses inside Claude Code, as a public toolkit.


There is a date to watch here. The deprecations page lists Sonnet 4.5's tentative retirement as "not sooner than September 29, 2026," which is one year after launch. That floor date arrived on September 29, 2026. As of that date, Anthropic lists the model as Active and has announced no deprecation, and the policy is at least 60 days of notice before any retirement of a publicly released model.


### October 15, 2025: Haiku 4.5


Haiku 4.5 arrived two weeks after Sonnet 4.5 at $1 input and $5 output. Anthropic said it delivers coding performance similar to Sonnet 4 at one-third the cost and more than twice the speed, and it scored 73.3% on SWE-bench Verified. It also framed a new orchestration pattern: a stronger model such as Sonnet 4.5 breaks a problem apart while several Haiku 4.5 instances handle the subtasks in parallel.


As of this writing, it is still the newest Haiku. Its own retirement floor is October 15, 2026, and the announced Haiku 5.5 is the model that will succeed it.


### November 24, 2025: Opus 4.5 and the price reset


Opus 4.5 launched at **$5 input and $25 output** , down from $15 and $75. That is one-third of the previous Opus price on both sides. Anthropic described it as "the best model in the world for coding, agents, and computer use," gave it a 200K context window, and introduced an **effort parameter** on the API so developers can trade speed and cost against capability. It launched across Claude apps, the API and all three major cloud platforms on the same day.


The price cut is the most consequential number in the 2025 ledger, because every Opus since has stayed at or below it. The full price history is charted in the pricing section below.


```text
THE 2025 PRICE RESET (Opus, per million tokens, input / output)    Opus 4    May 2025    $15 / $75   ##############################  Opus 4.1  Aug 2025    $15 / $75   ##############################  Opus 4.5  Nov 2025    $ 5 / $25   ##########  ___ one-third of the old price
```


### What 2025 taught the market


The release count rose from four to six, but the more important change was the target customer. The 2023 launches spoke to writers and researchers. The 2025 launches spoke to developers, then to anyone who wanted an agent to run for hours. If you compare how the rivals moved in the same year, the[best Claude alternatives](https://www.taskade.com/blog/claude-alternatives) guide ranks the field. By the end of 2025, Claude 1, Claude 2, Claude 2.1, Claude 3 Sonnet and both Claude 3.5 Sonnet versions had left the API, and the current family was the 4.5 generation.

## 2026: The Year the Cadence Broke


**Anthropic released eleven times between February 5 and September 28, 2026, more than in 2023 and 2024 combined.** Three things happened at once. The context window jumped to 1 million tokens, a new tier called Mythos-class appeared above Opus, and the gap between launches shrank to a matter of days.

### February 2026: Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 bring the 1M window


Opus 4.6 launched on February 5 at the same $5 and $25 price as Opus 4.5. Its headline change was a **1 million token context window in beta** on the developer platform, with premium pricing of $10 and $37.50 for prompts above 200K tokens. It supported up to 128K output tokens, added adaptive thinking that the model chooses to use, offered four effort levels, and brought agent teams to Claude Code. Anthropic reported a 76% score on the 8-needle 1M variant of MRCR v2, against 18.5% for Sonnet 4.5.


Twelve days later, Sonnet 4.6 arrived on February 17 at an unchanged $3 and $15 with the same beta 1M window. Anthropic said early-access developers preferred it over Opus 4.5 about 59% of the time, and it became the default model for Free and Pro users on claude.ai. The context history behind this jump, from 4K tokens to 1M, is in our[history of the context window](https://www.taskade.com/blog/context-window-history) and the[context window wiki entry](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/ai/context-window) .


### April 7, 2026: Claude Mythos Preview, the model Anthropic held back


Anthropic announced Claude Mythos Preview on April 7 alongside **Project Glasswing** , an effort to secure critical software. It described a general-purpose model that was strikingly capable at computer security, and said that over the prior few weeks it had used the model to identify thousands of zero-day vulnerabilities across every major operating system and web browser.


Launch partners included Amazon Web Services, Apple, Broadcom, Cisco, CrowdStrike, Google, JPMorganChase, the Linux Foundation, Microsoft, NVIDIA and Palo Alto Networks, and more than 40 additional organizations got access. Participants paid $25 and $125 per million tokens, and Anthropic committed $100 million in usage credits. It said it did not plan to make Mythos Preview generally available.


This is the first Claude model that Anthropic said it would not release generally, which is why the ledger lists it but a "latest model you can call" list does not. The tier it started is covered in[Claude Fable and Mythos explained](https://www.taskade.com/blog/claude-fable-mythos) .


### April 16 and May 28, 2026: Opus 4.7 and Opus 4.8


Opus 4.7 on April 16 held the $5 and $25 price and improved advanced software engineering. It accepted images up to 2,576 pixels on the long edge, more than three times what earlier Claude models accepted. It also shipped a new tokenizer: the same input can consume roughly 1.0 to 1.35 times more tokens, depending on content. Anthropic's pricing page says the tokenizer produces about 30% more tokens for the same text, so a price that did not change can still mean a bill that did.


Opus 4.8 on May 28 kept the price again. Anthropic said it was about four times less likely than Opus 4.7 to overlook flaws in its own code, added dynamic workflows for parallel subagents, offered fast mode at $10 and $50, and said it planned to release Mythos-class models "in the coming weeks" once cybersecurity safeguards were ready.


### June 9, 2026: Fable 5 and Mythos 5


Anthropic kept that promise on June 9. **Claude Fable 5** is a Mythos-class model made safe for general use, with safety classifiers that can decline requests. **Claude Mythos 5** is the same underlying model without those classifiers, offered only to approved Project Glasswing customers. Both carry a 1M token context window, up to 128K output tokens, and a price of $10 input and $50 output, less than half of Mythos Preview's $25 and $125.


What followed is the only launch in Claude's history that was suspended by a government. The sequence below comes from Anthropic's own timeline.


Anthropic said the controls required it to restrict access to foreign nationals, and because it could not verify nationality in real time, it suspended access for everyone on June 12. It said the trigger was a jailbreak found by Amazon researchers that let the model identify software vulnerabilities, a behavior the safeguards were meant to prevent, and that it trained improved classifiers in response. Fable 5 returned on July 1 across the Claude Platform, claude.ai, Claude Code and Claude Cowork.


For a release-date ledger, the lesson is that "released" and "available" can differ. Fable 5 was released on June 9, unavailable from June 12 to June 30 for most users, and back on July 1. The ledger keeps June 9, and this paragraph keeps the gap on the record.


### June 30, 2026: Sonnet 5 and the price that did not go up


Sonnet 5 launched on June 30 at **$2 input and $10 output** , below Sonnet 4.6's $3 and $15. Anthropic called it "the most agentic Sonnet model yet," said its performance approached Opus 4.8 at a lower cost, and made it the default for Free and Pro plans. It announced the $2 and $10 as introductory pricing through August 31, with a planned rise to $3 and $15 on September 1.


The rise never happened. Anthropic's pricing page now says the introductory price is the standard price and that the scheduled increase "will not occur." The launch price for Sonnet 5 is therefore still in force three months later.


### July 24, 2026: Opus 5


Opus 5 launched on July 24 at $5 and $25, with a fast mode that Anthropic described as 2.5 times faster at twice the base price. It said Opus 5 became the default model on Claude Max and the strongest model on Claude Pro. It also claimed state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks. As with every launch-day benchmark, read those as vendor claims, and check the[history of AI benchmarks](https://www.taskade.com/blog/ai-benchmarks-history) for how to weigh them.


### September 1, 2026: Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1


Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 launched on September 1 at the same $10 and $50 price. Anthropic said lower effort levels could match or beat Fable 5's results at much lower cost, cut the cache-read price to $0.25 per million tokens, and cut false positives in cybersecurity contexts by 60%. Fable 5.1 went to all platforms. Mythos 5.1 stayed restricted to vetted cyberdefenders and life scientists through trusted access programs.


### September 22 and 28, 2026: the 5.5 family


**Claude Opus 5.5** launched on September 22 at $4 input and $20 output, 20% below Opus 5, with cache reads at $0.20 per million tokens and a fast mode at $8 and $40. Anthropic called it the first model in the Claude 5.5 family, said it performs at Fable 5.1 levels while costing substantially less, and raised the five-hour usage limits on the Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans.


**Claude Sonnet 5.5** followed six days later, on September 28, at $2 and $10. Anthropic said it runs more than 30% faster than Sonnet 5 and costs up to 30% less for most work, and it scored 70.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, against 10.3% for Sonnet 5. Both 5.5 posts say the same thing about the last tier: Claude Haiku 5.5 will join the family "in the coming weeks."


Launch-day reaction was mixed, as developer reaction usually is. Hacker News commenters on Sonnet 5.5 noted it landed within two points of Opus 5.5 on CursorBench, at 55.5% and 57.8%. Another said Sonnet 5 had been poor value through the API next to cheaper open models. A third group complained that cybersecurity safeguards routed legitimate security work back to Opus 4.8, even with the Cyber Verification Program. Treat those as sentiment from commenters, not measurements.


That diagram shows a typical launch day in 2026, based on how the Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 4.5 announcements describe availability. The order of steps is illustrative. The verified fact is that recent models ship to the API, the major clouds and the apps on the same day.


### What 2026 taught the market


The 2026 ledger shows three shifts. Price stopped tracking capability upward: the Opus price fell from $15 to $5 to $4 across 2025 and 2026, and Sonnet fell from $3 to $2. Cadence collapsed: the shortest gap in the whole ledger, six days, sits at the end. And the top of the lineup became conditional. Fable classifiers, Mythos gating and cyber fallbacks mean the model that answers is not always the model you picked, which is the subject of the fallback section in[Claude models explained](https://www.taskade.com/blog/claude-models-explained) .

## Retired Claude Models: What Still Works and What Does Not


**Fifteen Claude models are active on Anthropic's API as of September 29, 2026, one is deprecated, and every model from Claude 1 through Opus 4.1 is retired.** A retired model fails: requests to it return an error, so any application pinned to one has to migrate. Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud set their own retirement schedules, so a model that is retired on Anthropic's API can still run on a partner cloud.


Anthropic uses four lifecycle terms, and they only move forward.


Active means fully supported and recommended. Legacy means the model no longer gets updates and may be deprecated later. Deprecated means still functional but not recommended, with a replacement and a retirement date. Retired means requests fail.

How much did Claude cost at launch compared with now?


Claude Opus launched at 15 dollars input and 75 dollars output per million tokens in March 2024 and stayed there through Opus 4.1. Opus 4.5 cut the price to 5 and 25 dollars in November 2025, and Opus 5.5 now costs 4 and 20 dollars. Sonnet held at 3 and 15 dollars from March 2024 until Sonnet 5 dropped it to 2 and 10 dollars in June 2026.


When is Claude Haiku 5.5 coming out?


Anthropic has not given a date. The Opus 5.5 announcement on September 22, 2026 and the Sonnet 5.5 announcement on September 28, 2026 both say Claude Haiku 5.5, built for high-volume and cost-sensitive applications, will join the Claude 5.5 family in the coming weeks. Until it ships, Claude Haiku 4.5, released October 15, 2025 at 1 and 5 dollars per million tokens, is the current Haiku.


Can I use Claude in Taskade?


Yes, with your own Anthropic API key. The Anthropic Claude automation connector can ask Claude a question, read an image or extract structured data inside any Taskade automation, on Pro and up, and it bills to your Anthropic account. On Pro and up, you can add your own Anthropic key so AI agents that name a Claude model run on it. Taskade Genesis itself runs on frontier models from top AI labs, with Auto as the default.
